summary: Practise decision trees, Markov models, ICERs, sensitivity analysis and DICE simulation. Review the course outline and see if it fits your needs.
lede: Cost-effectiveness modelling compares the costs and outcomes of health interventions to support resource-allocation decisions. For health economists, analysts and programme evaluators, the training develops skills to specify decision trees and cohort Markov models, calculate and interpret ICERs and net monetary benefit, test uncertainty through sensitivity analysis, and introduce DICE simulation and transparent reporting of findings.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who evaluate health interventions, prepare economic evidence or use cost-effectiveness findings to support programme and financing decisions.
audience: Health programme planners using economic evidence
